**Rabobank begins migrating iDEAL to Wero in major test for EPI**

*One of the Netherlands' largest banks is shifting its iDEAL payment traffic onto the European Payments Initiative's Wero platform, providing the first significant test of whether EPI can absorb a dominant national payment scheme at scale.*

Rabobank has selected ACI Worldwide to power its migration of iDEAL transactions to Wero, the account-to-account instant payment system backed by EPI. iDEAL processes the vast majority of Dutch e-commerce payments, making this one of the highest-volume national schemes to move onto Wero's rails.

The migration matters beyond the Netherlands. EPI's strategy depends on persuading banks to replace entrenched domestic schemes with a pan-European alternative. iDEAL is a strong brand with near-universal adoption among Dutch consumers and merchants, so Rabobank's willingness to migrate is a meaningful signal of confidence. If the transition goes smoothly, it strengthens EPI's case to banks in other markets still weighing the costs of switching.

ACI's role as the processing layer for both this migration and EPI's broader merchant acceptance infrastructure, announced last week, positions it as a central piece of Wero's technical stack. The practical question now is execution: whether Rabobank can move high-volume, low-friction payment flows onto a new platform without disrupting merchants or consumers.

*Sources: [ACI Worldwide Powers Rabobank's Wero Instant Payments, Advancing Europe's Real-Time Payments Transformation](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/ACIW/aci-worldwide-powers-rabobank-s-wero-instant-payments-advancing-8hlk8ougsnvl.html) — Stock Titan | [Rabobank taps ACI Worldwide for Wero instant payments migration](https://www.streetinsider.com/Corporate%2BNews/Rabobank%2Btaps%2BACI%2BWORLDWIDE%2Bfor%2BWero%2Binstant%2Bpayments%2Bmigration/26649484.html) — StreetInsider | [ACI Worldwide Powers Rabobank's Wero Instant Payments](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/currencies/articles/aci-worldwide-powers-rabobank-wero-050000549.html) — Yahoo Finance*

**Verification of payee delays leave European instant payments exposed to fraud**

*Uneven implementation of verification of payee across European banks is creating a window for APP fraud to accelerate alongside the instant payments mandate, according to analysis by FinTech Global.*

As the SEPA instant payments regulation pushes all euro-denominated credit transfers towards real-time settlement, the accompanying requirement for verification of payee is not keeping pace. FinTech Global reports that many banks have yet to implement the name-matching checks that are intended to catch misdirected or fraudulently initiated payments before funds move irrevocably.

The gap is not hypothetical. The UK's experience with Faster Payments demonstrated that speed without pre-transaction verification creates fertile ground for authorised push payment fraud. European regulators included VoP in the instant payments regulation precisely to avoid repeating that pattern, but staggered compliance timelines mean some banks will be sending instant payments without the corresponding safeguard.

For payment service providers and their fraud teams, the practical implication is that the risk window is now, during the transition period when instant settlement is live but VoP coverage remains patchy. Banks that have implemented VoP will bear a disproportionate share of the friction, while those that have not may inadvertently facilitate fraud flows across the network.

*Sources: [VoP delays: the fraud risks banks can't ignore](https://fintech.global/2026/06/16/vop-delays-the-fraud-risks-banks-cant-ignore/) — FinTech Global*

**BLIK positions itself as Europe's payment sovereignty model ahead of EPI expansion**

*Poland's BLIK, which now handles the majority of domestic digital payments, is being held up as a template for how national payment schemes can coexist with — or resist — pan-European alternatives.*

Disruption Banking profiles BLIK's trajectory from a bank-consortium mobile payment tool to a system that dominates Polish e-commerce and peer-to-peer transfers, processing volumes that dwarf card-based alternatives in its home market. The piece positions BLIK alongside the digital euro and Wero as competing visions for European payment sovereignty.

BLIK's relevance beyond Poland lies in the strategic question it poses for EPI. Where Wero's model requires national schemes to be absorbed into a single European brand, BLIK demonstrates that a domestically owned, bank-backed system can achieve near-universal adoption without pan-European ambitions. For Polish banks evaluating whether to join Wero, BLIK's dominance makes the cost-benefit calculation different from markets with weaker national alternatives.

The tension between national success and European integration is not new, but it is sharpening as Wero signs up banks and the digital euro moves towards a potential launch. Markets with strong domestic schemes — Poland, the Netherlands, the Nordics — will be the hardest for any pan-European system to penetrate, and BLIK's example will inform how those negotiations play out.

*Sources: [Can BLIK Make Poland Europe's Payment Sovereignty Champion?](https://www.disruptionbanking.com/2026/06/16/can-blik-make-poland-europes-payment-sovereignty-champion/) — Disruption Banking*

**Switzerland extends open finance framework to cover pension data**

*Swiss financial infrastructure body SFTI has published a standard for digital pension certificates, expanding the country's open finance protocols into retirement savings for the first time.*

The Swiss Financial Technology Innovations association has introduced a new standard enabling digital exchange of pension certificate data, covering both vested benefits and Pillar 3a retirement accounts. The framework builds on Switzerland's existing open finance technical standards, extending API-based data sharing from banking and investment accounts into the pension system.

Switzerland has pursued open finance through industry-led standardisation rather than regulatory mandate, an approach that contrasts with the EU's legislative path under PSD2 and the forthcoming financial data access regulation. Adding pensions to the scope is a practical test of whether voluntary standards can drive adoption in sectors where data portability has traditionally been minimal.

For the broader European market, the Swiss move illustrates where open finance is heading once the initial focus on payment accounts and transaction data matures. Pensions, insurance and investment data are the next frontier, and Switzerland is among the first jurisdictions to publish concrete technical standards for pension portability. How quickly pension providers adopt the standard will indicate whether industry-led approaches can match the pace of regulation-driven ones.

*Sources: [Switzerland Introduces New Standard for Digital Pension Certificates](https://fintechnews.ch/roboadvisor_onlinewealth/swiss-digital-pension-certificate-vvs-sfti/84186/) — Fintech News Switzerland*

**EBAday poll finds 78% back data sharing as top fraud defence**

*A live poll at this week's EBAday conference showed overwhelming support among payments executives for cross-institutional data sharing as the most effective fraud mitigation tool, reinforcing pressure for regulatory frameworks that enable it.*

At EBAday 2026 in Barcelona, 78% of attendees polled identified data sharing between financial institutions as the most effective approach to strengthening fraud risk mitigation. The poll was conducted during afternoon sessions focused on actionable fraud management and payments technology.

The result aligns with a direction regulators are already moving. The EU's forthcoming payment services regulation includes provisions for fraud-related data sharing, and industry bodies such as the Euro Banking Association have been advocating for frameworks that allow banks to pool signals without falling foul of data protection rules. The gap between consensus and implementation remains wide, however. GDPR constraints, competitive sensitivities and inconsistent technical standards continue to slow progress.

A conference poll is not a market study, but the strength of the consensus among a senior payments audience is notable. It suggests the industry has moved past debating whether data sharing is desirable and is now focused on the practical and legal obstacles to making it work.

*Sources: [EBAday 2026: 78% consider data sharing most effective way to strengthen fraud risk mitigation](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/47936/ebaday-2026-78-consider-data-sharing-most-effective-way-to-strengthen-fraud-risk-mitigation) — Finextra*
